title: We Got to Sesame Street
summary: Josh and Chuck celebrate Sesame Street's long run, covering its origins in the mid-1960s War on Poverty and early childhood research, the Children's Television Workshop and Joan Ganz Cooney and Lloyd Morrissett, early casting and characters (including Jim Henson and the Muppets), controversies over characters like Roosevelt Franklin and Don Music, tackling tough topics such as death, disability, incarceration and homelessness, research on educational outcomes, international co-productions (Israeli-Palestinian, South African, Afghan, Arabic versions), the 2025 USAID funding cuts and HBO deal, fun facts about the theme song and Elmo, and a listener mail on libraries.
topics: Big Bird Mr. Hooper death episode

segments.title: Opening banter and Sesame Street overview
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the episode, mention related Jim Henson and Muppet episodes, and describe Sesame Street as a long-running children's show started in 1969 and broadcast in many countries with co-productions.

segments.title: Iconic characters and Emmy awards
segments.summary: Discussion of the original and later characters such as Big Bird, Grover, Kermit, Ernie, Oscar, Cookie Monster, Snuffleupagus, Telly Monster, and Elmo, plus the show's Emmy and Grammy wins.

segments.title: Origins: Great Society and early childhood research
segments.summary: The show's roots in the mid-1960s, tied to President Johnson's Great Society and a focus on disadvantaged children aged three to five and early childhood development.

segments.title: Joan Ganz Cooney, Lloyd Morrissett and the FCC's vasty wasteland
segments.summary: Cooney and Morrissett's 1966 dinner-party conversation about TV educating kids, Cooney's work at New York educational TV, and FCC chair Newton Minow's 'vast wasteland' critique.

segments.title: Carnegie grants, pitch, and the Children's Television Workshop
segments.summary: Morrissett's Carnegie Corporation role and grants funded research leading to a 1968 proposal; the Children's Television Workshop tested approaches with a diverse group of experts.

segments.title: Promotion and Jim Henson's puppets
segments.summary: Funding and promotion efforts including loudspeaker trucks, and Jim Henson's Muppet background, plus early research showing puppets and animation engaged kids.

segments.title: Puppet and human interaction testing
segments.summary: Child psychologists' concern about humans and puppets interacting was dropped after testing showed kids were not interested in adult-only segments; comparison to other kids shows.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Ad break before the premiere discussion.

segments.title: Premiere, ratings, and early guests
segments.summary: The show's November 1969 premiere, ratings and music success of Ernie's Rubber Ducky, early celebrity guests such as James Earl Jones and Carol Burnett, and the choice of the name Sesame Street.

segments.title: Diversity, cast changes and Roosevelt Franklin controversy
segments.summary: Early Black and white human cast, the Mississippi ban reversed after 22 days, Latino representation added in season three, and the controversial Roosevelt Franklin and Don Music characters.

segments.title: Representation of disabilities and tough topics
segments.summary: Introduction of a character with Down syndrome in 1978 and later characters dealing with homelessness, parental incarceration, and opioid addiction, with statistics on these issues in the US.

segments.title: Research on educational effects
segments.summary: Educational Testing Service study after season one, a 2013 meta-analysis of 24 studies across 15 countries, and a Kearney and Levine study comparing areas with and without the show, plus a quote calling it a MOOC.

segments.title: Conservative praise and transition to global versions
segments.summary: A National Review quote calling Sesame Street the one great thing from the Great Society, and transition to international versions.

segments.title: International co-productions
segments.summary: Localized versions: Israel's Oscar as Moishe Ufnik, Afghanistan's co-production and cultural adaptations, the Arabic name Alam Simsim, UK biscuit monster, Latin America's Abelardo, South Africa's Takalani Sesame with Kami, and the Israeli-Palestinian co-production with research on attitudes.

segments.title: Arabic version as counterterrorism and 2025 USAID funding cuts
segments.summary: Quote about the Arabic version as a weapon against extremism, its use in Syrian refugee camps, and the 2025 USAID cuts and funding impacts including layoffs.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Ad break and brief mention of Afghan version character Zari.

segments.title: Sesame Street tackles tough topics
segments.summary: The death of actor Will Lee as Mr. Hooper and the 1982 episode handling death and grief, the 1985 Snuffleupagus episode on child abuse, a 9/11-era episode, the firefighter fire episode, military families, natural disasters and the COVID-19 episode.

segments.title: Funding history, HBO deal and season 56 uncertainty
segments.summary: Funding decline since the mid-1980s, licensing revenue, the HBO deal that ended in December 2024, and the uncertain future of season 56.

segments.title: Fun facts, character poll, theme song, Tickle Me Elmo, and Cookie Monster
segments.summary: Poll of favorite characters, the origin of the title Open Sesame, the theme song credits, the 1996 Tickle Me Elmo craze, Elmo testifying before Congress, Julia, Pinball Count, and the 2005 Cookie Monster sometimes food change.

segments.title: Listener mail on libraries
segments.summary: A listener writes about librarians defending the First Amendment, including a teen room collecting LGBTQ books and school librarians helping immigrant families; hosts tie it to the episode.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts invite listener mail and close the episode.
